summary: Independent review of the two regression rows I requested after pinning #951, plus the database-evidence hardening I asked for. These are rows I asked for, so I treated the result as a claim I co-sign and verified by mutation rather than by reading the description. SLOTCLEAR1 and LIQPULL1 are both ARMED, both declare a benign and a recurrence polarity, and both are added to the logs-unreadable fail-closed list so an evidence failure poisons them rather than reporting a clean zero. Mutation matrix, 8 mutations, all 8 turned tests RED: liquidity early-pull never flagged (count<3 -> count<0) => RED 2; unmeasured cancel no longer fails closed (unknown=unmeasured>0 -> False) => RED; fresh-SELL refusal never recorded as recurrence => RED; a refusal after a real owner fill wrongly counted as the bug => RED; the two new rows dropped from the logs-unreadable list => RED; the fresh-SELL freshness window disabled => RED 2; the _query_database hardening reverted to the old isinstance form => RED 2; and, in the strategy itself, capturing the streak AFTER the reset instead of before => RED 5. That last mutation is the one that mattered: had the capture been placed after the reset, the new field would log 0 forever and LIQPULL1 could never come out false. I verified the ordering by hand first (capture at line 4179, reset at 4186) and the suite now pins it. My first mutation batch reported 'no tests ran' for every mutation; that was a void harness, not five clean results. The shell is zsh, which does not word-split an unquoted variable, so my two test paths were passed as a single bogus argument. I re-ran with the paths passed literally against a baseline of 73 tests. The strategy change is observational only: it captures state.resting_below_floor_bars before the reset and adds it to the two existing [V2-RESTING-CANCEL] and [V2-RESTING-EH-DISARM] lines. No control flow, no new branch, no threshold moved. I read the whole diff because this is the live trading core two days before Monday. I verified every regex against the real emit sites rather than trusting the descriptions, because a marker is not the mechanism and a symbol captured as 'sym=TNON' on one side and 'TNON' on the other would silently never join, leaving a row that cannot come out false. [V2-ATR-PROBE] emits sym= then ts_ms= then flip=, [V2-FLIP-OWNER-FILL] and [V2-RESTING-SLOT-CONSUMED] both pass a bare symbol immediately after the tag, and [V2-CW-STATE-PROBE] emits sym= then resting_below_floor_bars= then resting_active=. All four join on bare symbols and all field orders match the ordered .* in the patterns. I verified the denominator precondition on the live box rather than from the doc. SLOTCLEAR1 and the good-reset half of LIQPULL1 depend on fleet-wide probes; on v2 pid 1033922 both MAI_TAI_STRATEGY_SCHWAB_1M_V2_ATR_FLIP_PROBE_SYMBOLS and MACD_PROBE_SYMBOLS read '*', and the pid is unchanged from Saturday's deploy, so the rows will have a real denominator on Monday. My first attempt at this used the wrong unit name, returned pid=0, and printed 'NOT SET' from a fallback echo against a nonexistent path; that was a broken query, not a finding, and I discarded it. I also confirmed _reading treats evaluated<=0 as UNEXERCISED rather than OBSERVED_CLEAN, so an absent denominator degrades honestly. My follow-up 2 from the #951 review is genuinely closed: _query_database now rejects non-int and negative values via 'type(parsed[key]) is not int or parsed[key] < 0', and test_database_census_refuses_a_malformed_metric_payload turns red when the hardening is reverted, so the guard is no longer written-never-run. Controlled pair, full unit suite, sorted failure-NAME sets: base df03b4a 46 failed / 3755 passed, head 38b76f4 46 failed / 3771 passed, identical 46 names, zero new failures. The base matches #951's head exactly, as it should since df03b4a is #951 merged. The +16 delta reconciles exactly: collecting the two touched files directly gives 57 at base (42 watch + 15 liquidity) and 73 at head (57 + 16), a delta of +16 from 10 new watch test functions, some parametrized, and one new liquidity test. Gate: base is an ancestor of head, no rebase needed. Diff is scoped to the two watch files, the two test files, and the observational strategy logging, with 15 deletions that are the two rewritten log statements and the renumbered doc steps; no other doc or board rows touched. Doc correctly updated to 19 rows and the weekend steps renumbered so the probe check precedes the selftest. FINDING, recorded rather than blocked: the three-bar threshold is written in two places. The watch hardcodes 3 at line 525 and the strategy defines _RESTING_LIQUIDITY_CANCEL_BARS = 3. Both sides are tested independently against their own fixtures, but nothing asserts they are the same number, no test references the constant, and the watch does not import it. I proved the hazard: setting the constant to 4 fails only the strategy's own behaviour tests, which is exactly what whoever changes the rule would update, leaving the watch still checking 3 with the suite green. It would then read a genuine early pull at 3 as guard-working, failing toward a false clean. The operator moved this threshold from 1 to 3 on 09-11, so the drift is live rather than theoretical. Cheap fix: import the constant into the watch, or add one test asserting the two agree. Not a merge blocker, since today both are 3 and the watch is correct as it would deploy. CI: validate passed twice on this head.
